jobs.state_note: User resubmitted via the OLD LSF path (bsub < SubmitJob.sh, ttc preset, single node n0371, 64 ranks, queue braun) rather than the SLURM path -- this is a different submission mechanism than RunConverge.slurm. It got further than any prior attempt: wrote the first post file and started all 13 Catalyst scripts (confirming the path fix works here too), running for 638s before the OS OOM-killed it -- Max Memory hit 456GB against only 128GB requested (Delta -328GB). SubmitJob.sh has its own memory line commented out (###BSUB -R "rusage[mem=320]"), so it's the same root cause as the SLURM OOM: no real memory reservation. stderr also showed EquivMetricSurf attempting a 1,144,384-value texture buffer against a 65,536 hardware limit -- a likely contributor to the memory spike, from rendering all 13 Catalyst scripts simultaneously. Reported to user with a proposed fix (raise rusage[mem=...] in SubmitJob.sh); awaiting their decision -- same as the still-unresolved SLURM --mem question on RunConverge.slurm.

jobs.summary: Job 269785 ended via TERM_RUNLIMIT at the 2-hour short-queue wall limit (exit 140, not a crash) -- cycle 188, t=10.54us of the 4000us target, zero FATAL_ERROR for the entire run. Primary goal achieved: ParaView Catalyst is confirmed working under CONVERGE 5.0.2 for the first time ever on this project -- 9 of 10 registered scripts produced 22 real PNG frames apiece. XTPlot_Pressure remains the one holdout: it received the same 22 triggers as every other script (well past the ~20-call threshold that should have forced its first periodic save) but produced zero output and zero errors.
